cards.explanation: The reason Jesus gives is that theirs is the kingdom of God. He says, “Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.” Notice He says yours IS, not yours someday maybe. I once owned nothing but dust, so hearing that makes me want to hug somebody with my mustache, friends.

The word is laugh. Jesus says, “Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.” Same flip as the hunger line: now it's tears, then it's laughing. I like a promise that ends in laughing, friends, since that's my whole business.

Jesus tells them to rejoice and leap for joy. He says, “Rejoice in that day and leap for joy…” Leap, friends. Not nod politely, LEAP. I'd try it, but I'd have to take my gold base with me, and that's a whole production.
The answer is True. Jesus says, “…great is your reward in heaven.” That's said to the ones hated because of the Son of Man. Rejoicing has a reason attached, friends, and the reason is big.
The answer is False. Jesus says the rich “…have already received your comfort.” The key word is already. He doesn't say later, friends, He says already.

The answer is that they will mourn and weep. Jesus says, “Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.” It's the mirror image of the blessing for the weepers. Laughing now, mourning later, and the other way around for the ones who weep now.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “Woe to you when all men speak well of you…” It's the one woe about reputation instead of money or meals. It's a surprising line, since most of us would be thrilled to hear everybody say nice things.

The word is false. Jesus says, “…for their fathers treated the false prophets in the same way.” Back in verse 23 the fathers of the haters treated the prophets badly. Here, when all men speak well of someone, the fathers did that for the false prophets, friends.

Jesus tells them to love their enemies. He says it plain: “Love your enemies…” Not tolerate them, not put up with them. Love. He's talking to the ones who will listen, so I'm all ears and all mustache.

The word is Bless. Jesus says, “…bless those who curse you…” Look at the pattern, friends: love your enemies, do good to haters, bless the cursers, pray for the mistreaters. Every one of them is a kind move aimed at someone being unkind.
The answer is True. Jesus says, “If someone strikes you on one cheek, turn to him the other also.” It's a hard one, and He doesn't dress it up. I think this one hurts.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “…if anyone takes what is yours, do not demand it back.” That comes right after “Give to everyone who asks you…” Not an easy teaching, friends, but that's what He says.
The line is “Do to others as you would have them do to you.” You measure by what you'd want, not by what you got. Short line, friends, and it's all there.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “Even sinners love those who love them.” He says it right after asking, “If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you?” That's the point of the line, friends.

The word is nothing. Jesus says, “But love your enemies, do good to them, and lend to them, expecting nothing in return.” Nothing means nothing. No receipt, no payback, no IOU in the back pocket. That's how you tell it apart from what sinners do.

The answer is that He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked. Jesus says, “…for He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked.” That's what the Most High is like. It's a kindness that doesn't wait to be thanked, friends.

The answer is “Forgive, and you will be forgiven.” It's the third pair after “Do not judge, and you will not be judged.” and “Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned.” Three pairs, friends, same shape.

The reason is that the measure you use will be measured back to you. Jesus says, “For with the measure you use, it will be measured back to you.” That's the last reason He gives for giving so freely. Whatever size scoop you carry, friends, that's the scoop coming back.
